source_locator.role: External source proof paragraph for the finite-rectangle product-measurability argument; not local proof step2.1.
source_locator.quote: For each $\epsilon>0$, continuity gives an open-rectangle cover of $K\times K$ on each member of which $q_u$ varies by less than $\epsilon$; compactness gives a finite subcover. Disjointify its rectangles by successive differences and on each nonempty piece use a value of $q_u$ from its rectangle. These pieces are measurable in the product sigma-algebra, so this gives a measurable simple function within $\epsilon$ of $q_u$ everywhere. Taking $\epsilon=1/n$ and applying pointwise-limit measurability to the real and imaginary parts shows that $q_u$ is product-measurable.
